version.changelog:
- Added integration with 17 search engines (8 Chinese, 9 Global), including privacy-focused and knowledge-based engines.
- Supports advanced search operators, time filters, and site/filetype-specific searches.
- No API keys required for usage.
- Provides quick usage examples, documentation references, and DuckDuckGo bang shortcuts.
- Enhanced privacy with support for DuckDuckGo, Startpage, Brave, and Qwant engines.

llm.summary: This skill is a straightforward search-engine guide that sends user-chosen queries to listed external search providers and does not install code, persist itself, or request credentials.

dimensions.detail: External network requests to search engines are inherent to the skill, but queries may be logged or handled under each provider's policies.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer, dependency, executable script, or package-install step was found in the inspected artifacts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not contain prompt overrides or hidden agent-control instructions; some supporting documentation is Chinese-language and includes locale and safe-search parameter examples, so users should choose engines and filters deliberately.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, background worker, privilege escalation, credential access, local indexing, or memory modification behavior was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is multi-engine search, and the artifact content consists of URL templates, search operators, and web_fetch examples for that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with your search terms being sent to the selected search provider. Avoid sensitive personal, credential, medical, legal, or proprietary queries, and keep safe-search enabled when appropriate.
llm.findings:
[AE1] expected: The referenced international search guide was present and inspected in full; it contains search documentation and examples, not hidden execution logic.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-language supporting documentation and China/global engine labels are consistent with a multi-region search guide; this is a usability and disclosure note, not evidence of unsafe behavior.
[SQP-2] expected: Sending search terms to third-party search providers is core to the skill and visible in the URL examples, though users should be warned not to search sensitive data.
[SQP-2] expected: The safe-search disabling parameters are documented as search-engine options; they can expose inappropriate results, but there is no automatic unsafe execution.
